A module with no skills folder starts as it does today.\u0022,\u0022When an agent step\\u0027s agent names a skill, the skill it gets is the folder of exactly that name in the skills folder of a module switched on for the parcel\\u0027s project. A name is only ever looked up among the folders the daemon read; it is never joined onto a path.\u0022,\u0022An agent step whose agent names a skill that no module switched on for the project ships, or that two of them ship, pauses the flow run before any process starts, with a reason naming the skill (and, for two, both modules) and the lever to perform the step again, as an unknown credential profile does today.\u0022,\u0022A Claude Code session whose agent names skills receives each one\\u0027s whole folder where the CLI loads skills from under the arguments the adapter passes, on every process of the session, spawn and resume alike, and is offered whatever the CLI needs for the session to use a skill. A test on the adapter\\u0027s rendered arguments and files shows this for an agent naming two skills from two modules.\u0022,\u0022Reading any file of a skill a session was given is allowed by the session\\u0027s tool guard, which a test against \\u0060ToolGuard.Decide\\u0060 shows.\u0022,\u0022An agent that names no skill gets exactly the arguments, settings document, environment, and session files it gets today, which a test comparing them shows.\u0022,\u0022The scripted executor\\u0027s record of a spawn names each skill the session was given, so a test can assert on it without a real session.\u0022,\u0022No event, definition content, or content hash changes: every stored agent reads and hashes as it does today.\u0022,\u0022\\u0060docs/design/design.md\\u0060 says where a module keeps its skills, how an agent\\u0027s named skill is resolved, and what happens when it cannot be, in place of the sentence that skills stay vendor-native repo files referenced by name, and the module layout docs (the root \\u0060AGENTS.md\\u0060 and \\u0060ModuleArtifact\\u0060\\u0027s own description) name the skills folder.\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Phase 4, mechanism wave, of the core-first re-plan (\\u0060notes/core-first-replan-2026-11-12/plan.md\\u0060 section 4 item 26 and section 6). Nothing reads it after that: an agent naming a skill runs as though it named none.\\n- A module\\u0027s directory is read by \\u0060ModuleArtifact.ReadAsync\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/Modules/ModuleArtifact.cs\\u0060), which knows \\u0060module.json\\u0060 and \\u0060definitions/\\u0060 only; \\u0060RefuseStrayEntries\\u0060 polices \\u0060definitions/\\u0060 and nothing beside it. The daemon reads the directories at start in \\u0060DaemonHost.ImportModulesAsync\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/Api/DaemonHost.cs:334-352\\u0060), from \\u0060ComposedModule.Path\\u0060 and \\u0060DaemonOptions.ModulePaths\\u0060.\\n- Which modules a project has switched on is \\u0060Project.Modules\\u0060 / \\u0060Project.IsSwitchedOn\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Core/Projects/Project.cs:34,55\\u0060).\\n- The agent step is built in \\u0060FlowRunAdvancer\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/FlowRuns/FlowRunAdvancer.cs\\u0060, the \\u0060AgentStepRequest\\u0060 at line 725). The unknown credential profile pause just above it (around line 695) is the pattern for an unresolvable skill.\\n- The Claude Code adapter passes \\u0060--setting-sources \\u0022\\u0022\\u0060 and a \\u0060--tools\\u0060 list built only from the tool catalog (\\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/Executors/ClaudeCode/ClaudeCodeInvocation.cs:80-84,137,286-301\\u0060), so today no skill reaches a session even if its files were on disk. The installed CLI on this Mac (2.1.328) lists \\u0060--plugin-dir\\u0060 in its help, which may be the way in; whether skills it loads appear under the adapter\\u0027s other arguments, and what tool or permission rule the session needs to use one, must be confirmed against the CLI, and the adapter\\u0027s remarks should record the version it was confirmed against as they do for the other arguments.\\n- The tool guard (\\u0060ToolGuard.cs\\u0060, \\u0060ToolGuardRules.cs\\u0060) allows the work directory and the session\\u0027s conversation directory. Placing the skills inside the flow run\\u0027s work path keeps them readable for an unconfined agent today and for a confined one once confinement is enforced; \\u0060SessionFiles\\u0060\\u0027 description says the daemon writes nothing else into the work directory, and will need to say otherwise if that is the placement.\\n\\n## Non-goals\\n\\n- Shipping any skill in the software module or changing its agents\\u0027 \\u0060Skills\\u0060 lists; that is phase 5 content.\\n- Skills authored by people or held in the store (design section 15 defers them), and any \\u0060coa\\u0060 command for skills.\\n- Refusing at draft or import an agent that names a skill no module ships; the pause at the step covers it, since which modules a project switches on can change after the agent is published.\\n- Recording which skill content a session received (a hash on the answer event would be a shape change for the shape wave, not this task).\\n- Changing what the CLI loads from the operator\\u0027s own configuration.\\n\\n## Overlaps, for the orchestrator\\n\\nThis touches \\u0060ClaudeCodeInvocation.cs\\u0060 as the confinement enforcement task does, and \\u0060ModuleArtifact.cs\\u0060 as the trigger definition task does (a fourth kind folder). module\\u0027s directory may hold a \\u0060skills\\u0060 folder beside its \\u0060definitions\\u0060 folder, with one folder per skill named for the skill and holding a \\u0060SKILL.md\\u0060. The daemon reads it at start for every module whose directory it reads, whether composed or given through \\u0060DaemonOptions.ModulePaths\\u0060. An entry whose name starts with a dot is passed over, as it is in the definitions folder. A start whose module has a skills folder holding any other loose file, a skill folder with no \\u0060SKILL.md\\u0060, or a skill folder whose name is not a plain name (letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores) is refused with a reason naming the path. A module with no skills folder starts as it does today.\u0022,\u0022When an agent step\\u0027s agent names a skill, the skill it gets is the folder of exactly that name in the skills folder of a module switched on for the parcel\\u0027s project. A name is only ever looked up among the folders the daemon read; it is never joined onto a path.\u0022,\u0022An agent step whose agent names a skill that no module switched on for the project ships, or that two of them ship, pauses the flow run before its launch is recorded, so the spawn it counted stays unused and no process starts. The pause gives a reason naming the skill (and, for two, both modules) and the lever to perform the step again, as an unknown credential profile does today.\u0022,\u0022A Claude Code session whose agent names skills has each one\\u0027s whole folder written under \\u0060.coanda/\\u0060 in the flow run\\u0027s work directory, beside the session\\u0027s other files, and is passed whatever arguments the CLI needs to make those skills available to it. This holds on every process of the session: the spawn, a retry\\u0027s resume, and a resume after a daemon restart, which rebuilds the session from its record. The folders are written fresh before each of those processes, replacing whatever the session left there, and the daemon never writes or deletes through a link the session placed, as \\u0060SessionFiles\\u0060 treats its own files. A test on the adapter\\u0027s rendered arguments and files shows this for an agent naming two skills from two modules.\u0022,\u0022A session can use only the skills its agent names. The tools and permission rules it receives are those its agent\\u0027s tool set maps to, plus only what using a named skill requires, and with them the session cannot invoke any other skill the CLI loads, including those the CLI ships with. A test on the rendered arguments and settings document shows this, and the adapter\\u0027s remarks name the CLI version this and criterion 4 were confirmed against and how.\u0022,\u0022Reading any file of a skill a session was given is allowed by the session\\u0027s tool guard, which a test against \\u0060ToolGuard.Decide\\u0060 shows.\u0022,\u0022An agent that names no skill gets exactly the arguments, settings document, environment, and session files it got before this change. Every existing expectation in \\u0060ClaudeCodeExecutorTests\\u0060 and \\u0060ToolGuardTests\\u0060 passes unchanged, and a test shows that a no-skill agent\\u0027s rendered arguments and settings document hold nothing this change adds.\u0022,\u0022The scripted executor\\u0027s record of a spawn names each skill the session was given, so a test can assert on it without a real session.\u0022,\u0022No event, definition content, or content hash changes: every stored agent reads and hashes as it does today.\u0022,\u0022\\u0060docs/design/design.md\\u0060 says where a module keeps its skills, how an agent\\u0027s named skill is resolved, and what happens when it cannot be, in place of the sentence in section 9 that skills stay vendor-native repo files referenced by name, and it names the skills folder where sections 14.2 and 14.8 list what a module brings and what its artifact holds. \\u0060docs/node-configuration.md\\u0060, under \\u0022How a Claude Code session runs\\u0022, says what a session whose agent names skills receives and where its skill files are written. The root \\u0060AGENTS.md\\u0060, \\u0060ModuleArtifact\\u0060\\u0027s own description, and \\u0060SessionFiles\\u0060\\u0027 description (which today says the daemon writes nothing else into the work directory) name the skills folder and the skill files.\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Phase 4, mechanism wave, of the core-first re-plan (\\u0060notes/core-first-replan-2026-11-12/plan.md\\u0060 section 4 item 26 and section 6). Nothing reads it after that: an agent naming a skill runs as though it named none.\\n- A module\\u0027s directory is read by \\u0060ModuleArtifact.ReadAsync\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/Modules/ModuleArtifact.cs\\u0060), which knows \\u0060module.json\\u0060 and \\u0060definitions/\\u0060 only; \\u0060RefuseStrayEntries\\u0060 polices \\u0060definitions/\\u0060 and nothing beside it, and \\u0060Visible\\u0060 passes over dot entries. The daemon reads the directories at start in \\u0060DaemonHost.ImportModulesAsync\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/Api/DaemonHost.cs:338-356\\u0060), from \\u0060ComposedModule.Path\\u0060 and \\u0060DaemonOptions.ModulePaths\\u0060.\\n- Which modules a project has switched on is \\u0060Project.Modules\\u0060 / \\u0060Project.IsSwitchedOn\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Core/Projects/Project.cs:34,55\\u0060).\\n- The agent step is built in \\u0060FlowRunAdvancer\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/FlowRuns/FlowRunAdvancer.cs\\u0060). The unknown credential profile pause (around line 696) comes before \\u0060SpawnedAsync\\u0060 records the launch (line 740), which is why its counted spawn stays unused; it is the pattern for an unresolvable skill.\\n- The Claude Code adapter passes \\u0060--setting-sources \\u0022\\u0022\\u0060 and a \\u0060--tools\\u0060 list built only from the tool catalog (\\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/Executors/ClaudeCode/ClaudeCodeInvocation.cs\\u0060), so today no skill reaches a session. Its remarks record the CLI version they were confirmed against (2.1.318).\\n- \\u0060SessionFiles\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/Executors/SessionFiles.cs\\u0060) writes the session\\u0027s files under \\u0060.coanda/\\u0060 fresh and owner-only, removing rather than writing through a link the session left; the persona is rewritten before every resume (\\u0060ClaudeCodeExecutor.cs\\u0060, around line 327). A resume after a daemon restart rebuilds the session from its on-disk session record (\\u0060ClaudeCodeExecutor.cs\\u0060, around lines 545-583), so rewriting skill files before that resume needs the record to say which skill folders to write.\\n- In the software module\\u0027s worktrees, only \\u0060/.coanda/\\u0060 is hidden from git, through the clone\\u0027s \\u0060info/exclude\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Modules.Software/Repositories/ProjectClones.cs\\u0060, \\u0060ExcludeLine\\u0060). A place such as \\u0060.claude/skills/\\u0060 at the work directory\\u0027s root would show in \\u0060git status\\u0060 and could collide with a repository\\u0027s own tracked skills.\\n- The tool guard (\\u0060ToolGuard.cs\\u0060, \\u0060ToolGuardRules.cs\\u0060) refuses paths at or inside the node home or a Claude Code config directory, except the work directory and the session\\u0027s conversation directory.\\n\\n## What the installed CLI does (2.1.328)\\n\\n- \\u0060--plugin-dir \\u003Cpath\\u003E\\u0060 loads a manifest-less directory\\u0027s \\u0060skills/\\u0060 folder under \\u0060--setting-sources \\u0022\\u0022\\u0060, and the CLI names each such skill \\u0060\\u003Cdirectory name\\u003E:\\u003Cskill name\\u003E\\u0060, not by its bare name.\\n- The \\u0060Skill\\u0060 tool is absent unless \\u0060--tools\\u0060 names it. Once it is named, a session can invoke any skill the CLI has loaded with no permission rule and no denial under \\u0060dontAsk\\u0060, and the CLI loads about nineteen bundled skills of its own despite \\u0060--setting-sources \\u0022\\u0022\\u0060.\\n- \\u0060--disable-slash-commands\\u0060 removes the bundled skills, but also the plugin\\u0027s skills and the \\u0060Skill\\u0060 tool, so it cannot keep only the named ones.\\n\\nSo offering \\u0060Skill\\u0060 as it stands would let a session use skills its agent never named. Criterion 5 states the outcome and leaves the means to the build session: for example, delivering the named skills as readable files with no \\u0060Skill\\u0060 tool, or offering \\u0060Skill\\u0060 with settings that deny every other skill, confirmed against the CLI either way.\\n\\n## Non-goals\\n\\n- Shipping any skill in the software module or changing its agents\\u0027 \\u0060Skills\\u0060 lists; that is phase 5 content, and the software module\\u0027s build copy rule (which copies only \\u0060module.json\\u0060 and definitions JSON) is extended there.\\n- Skills authored by people or held in the store (design section 15 defers them), and any \\u0060coa\\u0060 command for skills.\\n- Refusing at draft or import an agent that names a skill no module ships; the pause at the step covers it, since which modules a project switches on can change after the agent is published.\\n- Recording which skill content a session received (a hash or module version on the launch would be a shape change for the shape wave, not this task).\\n- Changing what the CLI loads from the operator\\u0027s own configuration.\\n\\n## Overlaps, for the orchestrator\\n\\n- This touches \\u0060ClaudeCodeInvocation.cs\\u0060 and the tool guard, as the confinement enforcement task does. Neither is a dependency, but the two meet in behaviour as well as in text: confinement refuses paths outside the work path and tools other than the five file tools. Whichever merges second keeps a confined agent\\u0027s named skills usable under confinement.\\n- This touches \\u0060ModuleArtifact.cs\\u0060, as the trigger definition task does (a fourth kind folder under \\u0060definitions/\\u0060).
